0.summary: AI-written (Fable), reader of the turns already proved; nothing built, nothing run, hand arithmetic only. Main finding: a turn that comes about because of the fall, with no mark, reading or corrected rule handed in, is already in the package for give = 0 and units that leave themselves: WayOfUnits.two_units_iff proves TurningInTime's AloneOutside, turns, kept, uses and uses₁ from the units' needs (marked := level below the first unit's need, alone := id, kept := first unit gone). C5's course is that pattern with takers that multiply and a rest that gives. In order L, with the stock's giving g(0)=0 and a>0, the givers' gift folds into one giving g'(z) = g(z) + p*b*[a ≤ z], the level's step is RegimeMargin.step g' (use), and the course is an instance of TurningInTime.turns_in_time_iff on a carrier Nat (number of takers): marked := (· < m), alone := (k * ·), Kept := (· = 0), H₂ := p*t; with the stock giving nothing and b ≥ t > 0 its right side reduces to exactly C2 (ii)'s condition (what is left at the step the takers first go unmet meets a). But TurningInTime's exact laws ask a cap (Meets up to hi, Keeps within hi), and with b > t no hi exists, so the Lean covers only b ≤ t; b > t holds on paper only. Givers that take nothing (t = 0) fail the premise `within`. In order B the folded giving gives from nothing (FromNothing fails) and the dichotomy changes in kind: I give hand countermodels where order B never ends and order L ends. C2 (i) is false as worded for an unboundedly rising stock giving (countermodel g(z)=2z, k=2) and false in order B even with the stock giving nothing. C2 (iii) holds by a hand instance (start 17 ends, start 10 never ends) and there it is a consequence of turns_in_time_iff. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss is a different thing: a handed-in reading of a loss that accrues by premise; its Accrues fails for any level that can hold. "A loss on the favoured share lowering it" is PoolFromCourse.Borne.shapers_left, a built witness with a toll on a clock; neither is a cut-off by an unmet need. The three clocks are TurningInTime.turns_in_time_iff_before (T + 1 < N), ClosedCapture.Thinned.turned_iff (counts at the reading step) and PoolFromCourse.window_never_read (K ≤ N); C2 (ii)'s condition is a case of the first only. No theorem I read says, in one statement, that a multiplying line is removed by the fall it causes and the rest goes on; the two halves exist separately (LineOnAStock.line_ends and gone_after for the removal; WayOfUnits.two_units_iff and With.goes_on for removal plus the rest going on, at kids = self and give = 0).

findings.statement: Q1a. In TurningInTime's exact turns (turns_in_time_iff, turns_in_time_iff_kept_below, turns_in_time_iff_before) what responds to the falling level is the way's step at a marked level, and the response is handed in: which levels are marked, that the way after a marked step is of the kept kind, that the kind is kept, and its one standing use are all premises.
findings.evidence: TurningInTime.lean:362 `def AloneOutside (marked : Nat → Prop) (alone : W → W) (after : W → Nat → W) : Prop := ∀ w x, ¬ marked x → after w x = alone w`; :1073-1074 `(outside : AloneOutside marked alone after) (turns : ∀ w x, marked x → Kept (after w x)) (kept : ∀ w x, Kept w → Kept (after w x)) (uses : ∀ w, Kept w → use w = H₂)`; module docstring :235-239 "`AloneOutside` and the marks are given, not derived: which levels make a difference to the way is a premise of every law that uses them. `Kept` is kept by premise (`kept`), that a way after a marked step is of the kept kind is a premise (`turns`)". The overdraw before the turn is also given: :1078-1079 `(short₁ : RegimeMargin.Short giving H₁ y₁) ... (uses₁ : ∀ j, H₁ ≤ use (Law.orbit alone w j)) (below : x < H₁ + y₁) (high : x ≤ hi)`.

findings.statement: Q1b. On the lock's own types the response is a reading step handed in: a window [N, K) of levels, every step reading, and a reading hL that gives a corrected (`kept`) rule there; in the share variant the reading also sets the share. The docstring says the correction reaches the share because the reading sets it, not because the share falls.

findings.statement: Q1c. In the endings (rising_takes_all, ends_with_net_rising, locked_ends_rising, locked_ends_with_net_regime) nothing responds: not responding is a premise (`un`: no marked level meets the need), and the use's floor or rise is a premise. locked_ends_rising concludes the whole net ends with the lock still Locked; no part goes on.

findings.statement: Q1d. In WayOfUnits the response comes about inside the model: a unit whose need the level does not meet is not in the way after the step, the level falls under what the units present take, and the five TurningInTime premises are proved, not assumed. Needs and uses are parameters; no mark, reading or update is given. This is C5's "the turn is because of the fall" already proved for two units that leave themselves and give nothing.

findings.statement: Q1e. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss: the response is a reading of the loss, handed in, at a reading step handed in; the loss grows by premise whatever the share does. findings.statement: Q2a. In order L, with g(0)=0 for the stock's giving, a>0, p ≥ 1 givers and q takers, C5's course is a course of TurningInTime.pair and meets the form of turns_in_time_iff: carrier W := Nat (the number of takers), after n x := if m ≤ x then k*n else 0, use n := p*t + n*c, giving' z := g z + (if a ≤ z then p*b else 0), level step RegimeMargin.step giving' (use n), net cut at need a. Then marked := (· < m), alone := (k * ·), Kept := (· = 0), H₂ := p*t, H₁ := p*t + q*c; AloneOutside, turns, kept, uses, uses₁ hold by cases, as first_outside etc. do at k = 1. No window and no reading is needed: the mark is the takers' own need. The kept-below variants add nothing here, since the kind (no takers) is kept at every level (kept_or_marked's first case).
findings.evidence: Argument: while every earlier level is at least a the givers are all in the way (each leaves itself) and the takers number n_j with n_{j+1} = k*n_j if m ≤ x_j else 0, as WayOfUnits.course_twoWay (:486) shows at k = 1; some unit goes on exactly where a ≤ x (m > a), as goes_twoWay (:470); so the nets never end from the same starts, as unending_iff_carrier (:517). The L step (x - T) + g(x - T) + gifts gated on z = x - T is `RegimeMargin.step giving' T x` by RegimeMargin.lean:249 `def step (g) (H x) := (x - H) + g (x - H)`, because the givers present are the same p at every live step and takers give nothing. giving' 0 = 0 since a > 0. This transfer and fold are not in the Lean I read; two_units_iff (WayOfUnits.lean:580) is the case k = 1, p = q = 1, b = 0. Not checked by any program or build.
findings.bears_on: C5; C2 (ii); C4; frozen tests 3 and 4

findings.statement: Q2b. Premises C5's course cannot meet. (1) The cap: `meets` up to hi and `keeps` within hi. With the stock giving nothing and b > t, Keeps giving' (p*t) hi fails for every hi ≥ a + p*t (at x = hi the step gives hi + p*(b - t)), and for smaller hi the law's right side is never true; so the Lean's exact laws reach only b ≤ t (b = t is the one case where the givers alone hold). (2) `within : need ≤ H₂ + y₂` fails for givers that take nothing (t = 0 forces y₂ = 0, so a ≤ 0). (3) `below` with `uses₁` asks the start already under the point of no return of the initial use; it is met from every start exactly when sup giving' < p*t + q*c, and otherwise only from a later step (the takers' growth, not a standing overdraw, brings the fall). (4) One `giving` for every way: met only because the givers are always present while the net lives and their gift reads what is left; with a general `give : U → Nat`, givers of several needs, or takers that also give, the level's step is not `RegimeMargin.step giving (use w)`. (5) Section 6's window laws are about RuleCapture's lock; forced onto them (window [0, m), every step reading, the reading a rule that leaves takers nothing) `safe` quantifies over every way and fails unless c = hi + 1 ≤ m.
findings.evidence: RegimeMargin.lean:262 `def Meets (g) (H y hi) := ∀ z, y ≤ z → z + H ≤ hi → H ≤ g z`, :265 `def Keeps (g) (H hi) := ∀ x, x ≤ hi → step g H x ≤ hi`, :255 Short, :252 FromNothing. TurningInTime.lean:1075-1079 premises of turns_in_time_iff; docstring :273-275 "with one `giving` for every way and nothing given from nothing ... the way enters the level's step only through `use`"; :242-243 "these laws are sufficient conditions, and whether a line can go on where no `hi` and `c` meet them is not shown"; WayOfUnits.lean:119-120 "under a giving with no such `hi` at what the ways take, `unending_iff_holds` does not apply". Arithmetic for (1): x ≤ hi, x - p*t ≥ a gives step = x - p*t + p*b.

findings.statement: C2 (ii)'s condition, where the law applies: with the stock giving nothing and b ≥ t > 0, y₂ = a and H₂ + y₂ = p*t + a, and turns_in_time_iff's last conjunct `H₂ + y₂ ≤ level of the course as it was at T + 1` holds exactly where z_T = X_T - p*t - n_T*c ≥ a, that is, what is left at the step the takers first go unmet meets the givers' need. In general the exact condition is the level one step after that step at or above the point of no return H₂ + y₂ of the givers' way under giving', which is "what is left meets a" only in that sub-case; with b < t and the stock giving nothing the net always ends.
findings.evidence: If z_T ≥ a then X_{T+1} = z_T + p*b ≥ a + p*t; if z_T < a then X_{T+1} = z_T < a ≤ p*t + a. Short giving' (p*t) a holds as giving' z = 0 < p*t for z < a; Meets holds as p*b ≥ p*t for z ≥ a. For b = t all premises of turns_in_time_iff (TurningInTime.lean:1070-1091) are met with any hi ≥ x; for b > t see the cap. Hand instance, order L, stock giving nothing, a = 1, p = 1, t = b = 1, m = 10, c = 1, k = 2, q = 1: from 10 the levels run 10, 9, then 7, 7, ... (T = 1, z = 6 ≥ 1); the law's premises hold with H₂ = 1, y₂ = 1, H₁ = 2, any y₁, hi = 17.

findings.statement: C2 (iii): a higher start can end where a lower start never ends. In the same instance the start 17 ends (17, 16, 14, 10, 2, 0: T = 4 with sixteen takers, 2 - 1 - 16 leaves nothing) and the start 10 never ends; also 12 never ends and 13 ends. There it is a consequence of turns_in_time_iff, whose right side is on the course as it was and is not monotone in the start. No theorem I read states it; WayOfUnits.greater_need and more_use_on_first are the proved comparisons nearest it (in the need and in who takes, not in the start).
findings.evidence: Hand arithmetic as given; not run by a program. WayOfUnits.lean:793-798 greater_need `(order : n ≤ m) (more : m ≤ m') (nothing) (short) (meets) (keeps) (high : x ≤ hi) : «不穷» ... ([(m, h), (n, H₂)], x) → «不穷» ... ([(m', h), (n, H₂)], x)`; :867-873 more_use_on_first.

findings.statement: C2 (i) is false as worded. (a) Order L with a rising stock giving that has no ceiling: g(z) = 2z, one giver (a = 4, t = 1, b = 0), one taker (m = 4, c = 1, k = 2), start 10: the levels run 10, 24, 63, 174, 495, ... and every need is met at every step. (b) Order B with the stock giving nothing: one giver (a = 2, t = 0, b = 5), one taker (m = 1, c = 1, k = 2), start 5: every step ends at a level of at least 5, so the net never ends while the takers double for ever. With the stock giving nothing in order L it holds on paper (the takers' take grows as k^j, the level by at most p*b a step). The proved endings of a growing take all ask a ceiling.
findings.evidence: (a) x_{j+1} = 3*(x_j - 1 - 2^j); with y_j = x_j / 3^j, y decreases by (1 + 2^j)/3^j, in total 4.5 < 10. A simpler variant with no giver's take has the closed form x_j = 3^j + 3*2^j from 4, checked against the recurrence. (b) the gift is gated on the level before the take, which stays at least 5 ≥ a; next level = (x - T, truncated) + 5. Ceiling premise: TurningInTime.lean:670 `(keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)` in rising_takes_all; LineOnAStock.lean:904-907 line_ends and :928 way_ends ask the same `keeps`. Hand arithmetic only.

findings.statement: Orders L and B differ in kind, not by a shift, once givers are units. In B the gift is given whatever is left: along the live net the folded giving is g(z) + p*b at every z, so FromNothing fails, and TurningInTime's regime laws and WayOfUnits' comparisons all ask it. Example with no takers, one giver a = 1, t = b = 5: from the level 3, order L goes 3, 0 and ends; order B goes 3, 5, 5, ... and never ends. With b < t and p*b ≥ a, order B sits at p*b for ever from any level meeting a, where order L always ends.
findings.evidence: RegimeMargin.lean:252 `def FromNothing (g) := g 0 = 0`; TurningInTime.lean:1075 `(nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving)` in turns_in_time_iff, used in its only-if direction through regime_levels (:570); WayOfUnits.lean:1098 GivenFromNothing.greater_need_fails and :1114 more_use_fails prove two comparisons fail where something is given from nothing. Agrees with the earlier try's first false_or_empty item (report.json), reached here independently by hand.

findings.statement: Q3. turned_by_loss is not takers being cut off by an unmet need, and neither is "a loss on the favoured share lowering it". turned_by_loss concludes only that the rule in force does not favour one step after a reading step, from a reading that favours at no loss of N or more; nothing is removed and nothing is said of what goes on. Its premise Accrues (the loss rises by at least one at every configuration) fails for any level that can hold or rise, so C5's course is not an instance. The phrase on the direction page is PoolFromCourse.borne_falls and Borne.shapers_left: the share is lowered in proportion by a toll on a clock, borne by the carriers by construction, with nothing needed.

C5's first half without any reading is LineOnAStock.lean:685 gone_after `(closed : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u) ... (nm : no unit of the line met at step k) : ∀ j, k + 1 ≤ j → no unit of the line in the way at j` (statement opened, proof not).

findings.statement: Q3, what would join them and what stands between. A join needs one course in which the loss is the fall of a level that the favoured share's own draw brings about and the favoured share's step reads that level through a need. Between: (1) the lock's premise Raises forbids the share falling under a favouring rule, and closed_stays_closed asks it on the whole configuration, so a favoured share cut off by the fall is excluded by premise, not derived; (2) windowAfter's share steps by fA of the share and the rule only; (3) in the regime laws on the window the level's step is the regime's, not the window course's loss step, and the loss in ClosedCapture rises without bound while a level is bounded below and given to; (4) the lock's way has one need for the whole net, so nothing of it is left to go on. A dictionary exists for the growth phase: givers and takers while the level meets m are CarrierCounts.select under the fixed rule (k, 1), which favours, and the cut-off is the rule (0, 1); the lag is one step (the takers are present and take nothing for one step).

findings.statement: Q4. The three clocks as premises. (1) Before what is taken cannot come back: the first marked step T has T + 1 < N, N the first step the course as it was is below H₂ + y₂; equivalently the level at T + 1 is at or above H₂ + y₂. (2) While those who register still have weight: at the reading step at which the loss has reached its bound, the others are at least as many as the carriers. (3) Before it removes them: the readers of the loss stand only while the loss is below K, and where K ≤ N they are gone before they read. C2 (ii)'s condition is a case of clock (1) only: the level after the turning step against the point of no return of the way that remains. It is not (2), having no weights, nor (3); the removal in C5 is of those who draw, not of those who register. The removal of the givers at a (C2 (i): m ≤ a) has the shape of (3) with the sides exchanged; that is a reading.

findings.statement: Q5. A unit that draws removed by the fall it helps cause, with the rest going on, is proved for two units that leave themselves and give nothing: exactly when (two_units_iff), in a worked case (With: needs 9 and 1, taking 4 and 1, levels 9, 8, 6, 10, 12, 12; the first unit ends at 8 and the second goes on for ever), and its contrast (Against: taking 1 and 4, same levels to 6, then 4, 0). more_use_on_first says the more of the take is on the unit the fall removes, the line that went on still goes on. For a line that multiplies, the removal alone is LineOnAStock.line_ends with gone_after; that the rest then goes on is not stated there. For a share (the lock), none: locked_ends_rising ends the whole net with the lock kept, Drained.strong_undone has the favoured share's draw remove the readers and keep the lock, and Borne.shapers_left lowers the share by a loss it does not cause.

against_the_frozen_tests: Test 1 (no exact condition short of running the course): comes out not against, with a limit. In order L the condition is of turns_in_time_iff's kind: one inequality at the step after the takers first go unmet, on the course as it was (takers multiplying, never cut off) run up to that step and not beyond. With the stock giving nothing and b ≥ t > 0 it is z_T ≥ a, and X_j up to T has a closed form x + j*p*(b - t) - q*c*(k^j - 1)/(k - 1). The Lean states its condition on the course as it was and says the closed form of T is not stated (TurningInTime.lean:288-289). In order B the folded giving gives from nothing, the premise FromNothing of every regime law fails, and the dichotomy changes: hand examples where B never ends and L ends (giver a=1, t=b=5 from 3; and b < t with p*b ≥ a), and C2 (i) fails in B (giver a=2, t=0, b=5, taker m=1, k=2 from 5). findings.statement: Law.level is not, in general, the course of a two-unit line on a stock with giving (a giver unit and a taker unit each leaving itself), in order L or B. Four partings. (a) Kinds come back: Law's gate is `need ≤ level t` at each step, so a kind unmet at one step is active again when the level returns; in the line a unit whose need is unmet leaves no kids and is gone. (b) The taker's gate: Law's focal takes only while met; in the line `taken use w` totals every unit of the way at the step, met or not, so a unit takes once more at the step it goes unmet. (c) Law's draw and contrib are schedules in t; this one is not an obstacle, since U is any type and a lineage F_t with kids [F_{t+1}], use = draw t, give = contrib t carries a schedule. (d) Truncation: Law adds, then subtracts; the frozen L and B subtract (truncated), then add. In particular, with needF > needG and a draw beyond renewal, Law's focal goes unmet, the level rises by renew, and the focal returns: the very case C2 (ii) is about is where Law and the line differ most.

(d) Start 1, renew 1, needG 1, needF 0, draw 3: Law gives 1 + 1 − 3 = 0; take-then-give in order B gives (1 − 3) + 1 = 1.

findings.statement: The earlier try's phase lemma holds on paper. Premises: L.needF = 0; draw t = d and contrib t = c for all t; c ≤ d; H = d − c; g z = L.renew if L.needG ≤ z, else 0. Conclusion: for all t, L.level t = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step g H) (L.start + H)).state t − H. In the frozen file's terms: for these laws Law's level is what is left after the take, of the two-unit line in order L started at level start + d with the stock giving nothing (giver: need needG, use 0, give renew; taker: need 0, use d, give c), and the way stays the same as Law's active kinds because under c ≤ d the level never rises once below needG. So Law is order L exactly, read half a step apart. In order B, with Law's level read as the line's level, it agrees only while every take is covered by the level (for example where H ≤ needG).
findings.evidence: Write A x = x − H (truncated) and B z = z + g z. RegimeMargin.step g H = B∘A (RegimeMargin.lean:249). For needF = 0 Law's step is z ↦ (z + g z + c) − d, and (a + c) − d = a − (d − c) in truncated arithmetic when c ≤ d, so Law's step is A∘B. Then A((B∘A)^t x) = (A∘B)^t (A x) by induction on t, and A(start + H) = start. Instance checked by hand (the try's own): start 2, renew 1, needG 2, needF 0, draw 1: Law 2, 2, 2; the regime from 3 is 3, 3, 3; minus 1 gives 2. Order B parting, checked by hand (the try's countermodel): stock giving nothing, taker of 5 needing nothing, giver need 1 giving 4, from 4: order B gives (4 − 5) + 4 = 4 for ever; Law gives 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 and stays at 0. Not machine-checked by me.

findings.statement: Orders L and B agree up to the half-step shift wherever each step's take is covered by the level, and differ in kind where it is not. For a way that stays the same with total take T and gated giving G: B on the level is x ↦ (x − T) + G(x) and L on what is left is z ↦ (z + G(z)) − T; with no truncation both are v ↦ v + G(v) − T. With a changing way the shift is not constant: L on what is left subtracts the next way's take, B the present one's. Where T exceeds the level, B gives from nothing left: givers alone (need a, use t, give b, n of them) follow x ↦ (x − nt) + nb·[a ≤ x], which stays at nb for ever whenever a ≤ nb, even with b < t (a = 1, t = 5, b = 1, n = 1: from 1 the level is 1 for ever), while in order L the same way ends. So B's condition for going on is not L's condition shifted.

2.what_i_would_try: Three, and for each I say plainly that no October proof gets shorter by it. (1) The phase lemma. Premises: L : RelationalRenewal.Law; L.needF = 0; L.draw t = d and L.contrib t = c for all t; c ≤ d; H = d − c; g z = if L.needG ≤ z then L.renew else 0. Conclusion: for all t, L.level t = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step g H) (L.start + H)).state t − H. Proof: the conjugation A∘(B∘A)^t = (A∘B)^t∘A with A x = x − H, B z = z + g z. It lets RegimeMargin's point of no return speak of this family (with 0 < H ≤ renew: going on from starts at or above needG by Adjusted.holds_from, RegimeMargin.lean:661; ending below by ends_below, :705), a boundary Law does not state. Older theorem that would become a case: none whole. Only the restrictions to this family of no_return_below_support (RR:357, proof 15 lines), permanently_below (RR:376, 4 lines), overdraw_crosses_support (RR:387, 27 lines) and within_renewal_sustains (RR:325, 7 lines); the general proofs stay. It is a proved link between a foundation module and RegimeMargin, not a shortening. (2) The conjugation itself on the spine, once: for any A, B : S → S and x, Law.orbit (A∘B) (A x) n = A (Law.orbit (B∘A) x n). The phase lemma and `order B on the level is order L on what is left wherever each take is covered` are both cases of it. I did not open Lasting, LastChange or BandRest, so it may already be there under another name; no older proof known to me becomes a case. (3) The turn, in order L. Premises: stock giving nothing; givers with need a, use t, give b, kids = the unit itself, n ≥ 1 of them; takers with need m > a, use c, kids = k takers; s the first step with level x_s < m; z_s = x_s − (total use of the way at s). Conclusion: the net never ends iff b ≥ t and a ≤ z_s. The tail after s is Adjusted.holds_from and ends_below under g(z) = n·b where a ≤ z. Older theorem that would become a case: none in what I read (Law's gates are memoryless and its pulses have the roles reversed). Whether LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds, which I did not open, becomes its case at give = 0 is for the reader of the line to say. If not, it is a piece added beside the others and should be landed as that. Before any of the three: order B should be dropped or named as a different model, since it gives from nothing left.

What came back: (1) In order L the guesses C2 and C3 hold in a sharpened form: with 1 <= m <= a the net ends from every start (0 exceptions); with m > a the outcome is decided by one number at the step the takers first go unmet, what is left there (z* = x* - G*t - N*c): for g = 0 the net never ends exactly where b >= t and z* >= a (354,240 of 354,240), and for a rising stock giving exactly where the configuration at the next step holds in the line's sense, with y the root of g(z) + G*b*[a <= z] against the take (43,200 of 43,200 for each of eight givings). C2 (ii) as worded ("what is left still meets the givers' need") is necessary but not sufficient at g = 0 (it omits b >= t) and is neither with a stock that gives. (2) Order B is a different model in kind, not a shift: it is the line with "nothing given from nothing" dropped. There C2 (i) is false (the net never ends exactly where x >= a and G*b >= a, the takers doubling without bound at a resting level), and with G*b >= a and m > a the takers make no difference at all. Only where G*b < a and b >= t is B a shift of L (z* + G*b >= a in place of z* >= a). Every run that never ends in L never ends in B (3,757 of 3,757). (3) The least "higher start ends, lower never ends" pair has give = 0 and t = 0: it is already in the plain line on a stock, so C2 (iii) and the dichotomy are not brought by giving; what giving adds in L is that units which take something (t >= 1) can go on without end with no stock giving, exactly where b >= t and x >= G*t + a. (4) For a way of givers only, the L step is literally RegimeMargin.step with giving renamed to g(z) + G*b*[a <= z], so C3 is the line's Holds region under a renaming, except that where b > t the level rises without bound and the premise Keeps of unending_iff_holds fails at every useful hi. (5) C1 held in 16,640 of 16,640 random steps and holds because after never reads the level's law.

The tail of C2 (ii) after the takers are gone is `ends_iff_below` (:741) verbatim only where b = t: `meets` needs b >= t and `keeps` (Keeps g' H hi) needs b <= t, since for b > t the level rises by (b - t)*NG a step and passes every hi; for b > t the two halves are `ends_below` (:705) and `Adjusted.holds_from` (:661, no top), and `LineOnAStock.Regime` (:193) with its one hi does not hold. findings.statement: C2 (ii), order L, g = 0, m > a, c >= 1, a taker in the way: the net never ends exactly where b >= t and, at the first step j at which the takers' need is unmet, a <= z_j = x_j - t*NG - c*n_j (what is left there meets the givers' need). Equivalently all that is taken at that step is at most x_j - a, less than the gap m - a between the two needs, so the takers must fall while few. From the start numbers alone: X_0 = x0, X_(i+1) = X_i + (b - t)*NG - c*n0*k^i while X_i >= m; j the first i with X_i < m; never ends iff b >= t and a + t*NG + c*n0*k^j <= X_j. This is a condition at one step, not 'the level never falls below a'.
findings.evidence: s2_ii_iii_wide.out: order L, g = 0: 153,600 cases (ranges of the previous finding), 11,140 never end, condA mismatches 0; closed form against the simulated fate over x0 0..59: 230,400 cases, 0 mismatches (s2_two_kinds.py closed_form). On paper I have the argument (after step j only givers remain; with b >= t and z_j >= a the next level is at least a + t*NG and what is left never falls; with z_j < a the next level is z_j < a; with b < t and t >= 1 the level falls by (t - b)*NG a step), so 'follows on paper' is also fair; the searched range is what I can vouch for line by line.

findings.statement: Once the stock gives of itself, 'what is left at that step still meets the givers' need' is not the exact condition of C2 (ii); the exact condition found is that the givers are met at step j and the configuration at step j+1 holds (`Holds` with y the least level where g' meets the givers' take). For a rising g this follows on paper (the givers' step is then monotone in the level); for min z (12 - z) it held in search only.

findings.statement: C2 (iii) is true and needs no giving. The smallest world found has a 'giver' that gives nothing and takes nothing; it is of the kind of `HigherStartEnds` (:1840) with two kinds and a stock that gives nothing. With a giver that takes and gives: a = 1, m = 4, t = 1, b = 1, c = 1, k = 2, one of each, g = 0, order L: from 3 the levels are 3, 2, 2, 2, ... (never ends); from 4 they are 4, 3, 0 (ends at step 2). There is no threshold in the start: along x0 = 0..59 the fate changes up to 4 times. It does not occur with m <= a in either order (0 worlds).
findings.evidence: s2b.out (order L, g = 0, wide ranges): worlds with a never-ending start below an ending one: 372 with b = 0 and t = 0, 1,116 with b >= 1 and t = 0, 900 with b >= 1 and t >= 1. Smallest overall: a = 1, m = 3, t = 0, b = 0, c = 1, k = 2: from 2 level 1 forever, from 3 levels 3, 2, 0. Fates over x0 = 0..59 for a = 1, m = 7, t = 1, b = 1, c = 1, k = 2: eeeNNNNNeNeee... (N never ends, e ends). The two courses by hand agree with run2's output.

findings.statement: Orders L and B differ in kind, not by a shift, where the givers' total gift meets their own need. Order B, g = 0, m > a, where the takers do go unmet at a step j: never ends iff a <= x_j and (b*NG >= a, or b >= t and z_j + b*NG >= a). The second branch is the L condition shifted by the gift; the first asks nothing of what is left. In B the takers can also never go unmet (level pinned at the gift, at or above m), and a way can go on taking more than is given: a = 1, m = 2, t = 2, b = 1, one giver: level 1 forever with take 2 and gift 1. On a fixed way B's gate folded into the stock is g(z) + b*NG*[a <= z + take], which gives from nothing where a <= take, so `FromNothing` fails.
findings.evidence: s2_ii_iii_wide.out, order B, g = 0: 153,600 cases, 92,309 never end, of which the takers never go unmet in 13,360; condB mismatches 0 where they do; the L condition mismatches 67,809. s2_ii.out (narrow ranges, t up to 2): 'Holds at j+1' with the shifted gate fails in 776 of 17,280 in order B, first at a = 1, m = 2, t = 2, b = 1, c = 1, k = 2, start 1. I did not open RelationalRenewal, so I cannot say whether B is October's order; the 16 November report says October's taker takes only while met, which B here does not do.

findings.statement: Left, and not a renaming (1): givers that also leave givers. Order L, any stock g, any kinds: if every unit has a kid, kids need no more than their parent, and every unit gives at least what its kids together take (taken use (kids u) <= give u), then from a configuration whose way is not empty and where what is left after the take meets every need (need u <= x - taken use w), the same holds at every later step, what is left never falls, and the net never ends, though the way may grow without bound. Argument: all are met and all give, so the next level is z + g(z) + total give >= z + taken of all the kids, and the kids need no more. For one kind (need a >= 1, use t, give b, leaving k of itself, N of them at level x) on a stock that gives nothing it is exact: never ends iff b >= k*t and a <= x - t*N. So b against k*t separates a line that grows and ends from one that grows and goes on. With kids u = [u] it is `Holds` at y = the greatest need, a renaming; with k >= 2 it is not: the gift goes with the number present, `left_of_taken` fails, and `need_unmet`'s `keeps` cannot hold since the level is unbounded.
findings.evidence: s3.out (d): 43,689 random starts in the region (1 to 3 kinds, needs 0..5, uses 0..3, gives 0..6, one or two kids, four g): 0 left it or had what is left fall within 12 steps; 19,924 ways grew. (c): one kind, a 1..4, t 0..3, b 0..8, k 1..3, N 1..3, x 0..24, g = 0: 32,400 cases, 17,568 never end, 0 mismatches with (b >= k*t and a <= x - t*N). Worked: need 1, use 1, give 2, leaving two, from one unit at 2: (number, level) = (1,2), (2,3), (4,5), (8,9), (16,17), (32,33), (64,65). With a stock that gives the condition is sufficient only: false but never ending in 975 (hump12), 795 (min(z,3)), 975 (z) of 21,600; true but ending 0. The unitwise premise is not necessary either: two givers (t = 0, b = 1) and one taker (c = 1), each kind doubling, level 2^j + 1, never ends though the takers give nothing; what matters there is the way's whole gift against the next way's whole take. Whether October's modules already state this I cannot say: not opened.

findings.statement: Left, and not a renaming (2): a giver once unmet is gone for good and its giving with it, though the level come back; the same giving folded into the stock comes back with the level. The fates can differ. That the unit does not return is `never_in` / `gone_from` (LineOnAStock.lean:664, :674) at the givers' line; what is added is only that the gift is a total over the units present.

against_the_frozen_tests: Test 1 (no exact condition in C2 (ii) short of running the course): does not come out against it for a stock that gives nothing in order L. The condition is b >= t and a <= x_j - t*NG - c*n_j at the first step j the takers are unmet, and it has a closed arithmetic form in the start numbers (0 mismatches in 230,400 cases). Where the stock gives of itself, the exact condition found is `Holds` at step j+1 (0 mismatches for five givings), which needs the course run up to that step and no further: the same shape as `unending_iff_holds`' 'the course comes to a configuration that holds'. There is no threshold in the start level (the fate changes up to 4 times along x0 = 0..59).

Test 2 (the dichotomy differs in kind between L and B): it does. C2 (i) holds in L with repairs (0 of 28,800 never end at g = 0) and fails in B (9,840 of 28,800 never end; exactly where b*NG >= a and x0 >= a). In C2 (ii) the B condition is the L condition shifted by the gift only where b*NG < a; where b*NG >= a nothing is asked of what is left, takers can go on doubling forever on a level that is the gift, and a way can take more than it is given without end. As frozen for both orders the claim is about the order; as a claim about order L alone it stands.

Test 3 (every statement that holds is an existing theorem under a renaming): for the world of C2 as frozen, in order L with takers needing at least what givers need, the way with givers is the Lean's own course under g'(z) = g(z) + b*NG*[a <= z], configuration for configuration (on paper; 0 differing courses in 5 x 184,320 and 35,071 more). So there C1 is `ways_alike`, C3 is `Holds`, C2 (i) is `fall` after `rise`, the tail of C2 (ii) is `ends_iff_below` where b = t, and 'what is left meets the givers' need' is `root_above_need` where t >= 1 and g gives nothing below a. Not existing theorems, though still statements about the line on a stock with no give in them: the exact condition of C2 (ii) from the start (a mixed way; the module says it has none, :96-98 and :120), and a no-top form of the holding half for b > t (`Regime`'s one hi fails). Outside the renaming: givers that leave givers, and a giver lost for good when the level returns.

Test 4 (no older proof would become a case and get shorter): on my evidence none would. A general alikeness over any level law has `ways_alike` (:547, proof 6 lines) as its case at the same length. The mixed-way law would be proved from `fall` or `line_ends` and `unending_iff_holds`, shortening neither. The covered region for multiplying givers has at most `Adjusted.holds_from` (RegimeMargin.lean:661) as a neighbour, and the band form used by `unending_iff_holds` is not its case. Each would be a piece beside the others.

Test 5 (C2 (ii)'s condition is its own conclusion handed in): it is not. It is a condition on one step (what is left at the step the takers first go unmet, or `Holds` at the next), not 'the level never falls below a'. `unending_iff_holds`' premise `along` (a regime at every way the course reaches) is the nearest thing to a handed-in premise, and for b > t it cannot be given at all.

Test 6 (C1 false, or true only because `after` never reads the level's law): the second. 0 violations in 40,000 pairs of courses with give, and 0 in 40,000 pairs of level sequences that come from no law (22,806 with the hypothesis holding). It is the alikeness law with one more thing that makes no difference to it. What it leaves unsaid: with give the level no longer reads the way only through what it takes, and in order L which units give is read on what is left, finer than which needs are met.
5.what_i_would_try:
Three, in the order I would weigh them; none makes an older proof shorter, and I say so.

1. The covered region for units that give and multiply (order L; a new definition of the level with give is needed). Premises: `some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []`; `down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u`; `covers : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) ≤ give u`; any giving g; a configuration (w, x) with w ≠ [] and ∀ u ∈ w, need u ≤ x - taken use w. Conclusion: at every step n the way is `generation kids n w`, every need of it is at most what is left there, what is left at step n+1 is at least what is left at step n, and the net never ends. With it, for one kind and g = 0, the exact form: never ends iff b ≥ k*t and a ≤ x - t*N (needs a ≥ 1). No older theorem becomes a case: at give = 0 `covers` forces kids that take nothing. Its nearest neighbour is `Adjusted.holds_from` (RegimeMargin.lean:661, 9 lines), which it does not contain. It is the one statement here that places a growing line that ends against a growing line that goes on by one comparison (give against the kids' take), and it should be landed, if at all, as a piece beside, not as a join.

2. The mixed way on the line on a stock as it is (no give): a closed line S of one need m whose units' kids of the line take more than the unit, beside units that leave exactly themselves; giving bounded with giving 0 < m (or `Keeps giving 0 hi`), and a regime for the ways of the remaining units as in `unending_iff_holds`. Statement: the net never ends iff there is a step k, some need met at every step before it, at which no unit of S is in the way and the configuration holds (`Holds`). It would be proved from `fall` (:773, 6 lines) or `line_ends` (:904, 9 lines) and `unending_iff_holds` (:1239, about 40 lines), so those are used, not shortened; `unending_iff_holds` is its case with S empty only in statement. It fills what the module says is not there (:120), and C2 (ii) with b = t is its instance under g'. For b > t it first needs a form of `Regime` without the one top hi.

3. Alikeness over any level law: for any `left left' : List U → Nat → Nat`, two start levels and one way, if the levels of the two orbits of `TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) left` and `... left'` meet the same needs of the first way at every step before n, the ways agree up to n. `ways_alike` (LineOnAStock.lean:547, proof 6 lines, :553-558) becomes the case `left := LineOnAStock.left g use`, at the same length. Worth doing only if a level with give enters the package, so that C1 is said once for every order; by itself it adds nothing.
